A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BA-LoRA research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v4 reports original NLG and NLU benchmark results, component ablations, rank experiments, feature visualizations and computational-cost measurements.

after.justification: v5 retains original benchmark and ablation results and reports additional coefficient-sensitivity results and replacement computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains PiSSA initialization, all three regularizers, and their NLU/NLG loss definitions. The new schematic and disclosure that adapters cover all linear layers do not establish an algorithm change; revised coefficient values are experimental settings.

E1.justification: Mathematical reasoning, code generation, instruction following, and GLUE/GLUE-X coverage remain unchanged. The new sensitivity and replacement cost experiments reuse existing MetaMathQA/GSM8K coverage; DeBERTa/GLUE evaluation remains elsewhere.

E2.justification: The replacement cost comparison in Appendix D.1 adds Full FT alongside LoRA, PiSSA and BA-LoRA in Table 10. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark tables and analyses is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes NLU λ2 from 0.04 to 0.01 and NLG (λ1, λ2) from (0.0001, 0.3) to (0.00001, 0.1). Appendix C.4 adds controlled coefficient sweeps. D.1 replaces DeBERTa-v3-base/full-GLUE profiling with LLaMA-2-7B on the first 100,000 MetaMathQA examples using ZeRO-2. These reported changes do not establish that retained benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4/Figure 6 adds sensitivity analysis of the three regularization coefficients on LLaMA-2-7B/GSM8K, and D.1 revises the resource-cost analysis. Existing component ablations, OOD evaluations, LoRA-variant analysis and t-SNE studies remain. The rank study moves from Section 4.4/Figure 1 to Appendix C.3/Figure 5.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three independent runs in Section 4.2, three GLUE seeds in Appendix B.4, and the same uncertainty-reporting practice. v5 reiterates three-run averaging for costs in D.1. Corrections to uncertainty magnitudes in Table 1 change numerical results, not the statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 corrects four uncertainty magnitudes, including LLaMA-2-7B BA-LoRA MATH from 9.21±17 to 9.21±0.17; benchmark means remain unchanged. Figure 6 adds sensitivity curves favoring λ1=0.00001 and λ2=λ3=0.1. D.1 replaces DeBERTa/GLUE costs, including BA-LoRA's 15.82 hours/7.1 GB, with LLaMA/MetaMathQA costs of 5 hours 41 minutes/40.68 GB. These are different settings, not demonstrated efficiency gains.

T1.justification: The decomposition, covariance, KL, entropy, SVD-ratio and total-loss mathematics remain unchanged. The displayed LoRA forward equation becomes inline prose, and subsequent equations are renumbered. No substantive assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about mitigating catastrophic inheritance and improving NLU/NLG performance. Removing the introductory experiment summary and shortening the conclusion do not materially change claim scope.

C2.justification: Section 3.2.3 reframes KLD's rationale from preserving generation style/coherence to balancing retained knowledge with downstream performance. Appendix C.4 interprets coefficient sensitivity. New D.3 makes limitations explicit, largely developing existing D.2 concerns, including unexplored societal bias and potentially suboptimal fixed regularization weights.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly specifies adapters on all linear layers and revises coefficient values. Appendix D.1 documents DeepSpeed ZeRO-2 and the first-100,000-example selection for its replacement profiling experiment. Code and model access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 adds Rasley et al. (2020) on DeepSpeed for the implementation described in Appendix D.1. The related-work survey and positioning of BA-LoRA relative to PiSSA and other PEFT methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction condenses the LoRA explanation and removes its experiment-preview paragraph. The rank discussion moves to the appendix, main analyses are regrouped under Section 4.3, and the cost discussion is rewritten. New sensitivity and limitations subsections are localized additions; most prose and structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v5 adds a framework schematic (Figure 1), coefficient-sensitivity plots (Figure 6), and a cost table (Table 10) replacing the earlier cost bullet list. The original rank plot becomes appendix Figure 5. Existing plots and tables are otherwise retained with local relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The framework diagram, sensitivity analysis and more explicit implementation/resource reporting modestly improve clarity and transparency. Benefits are limited by replacing the earlier NLU cost evidence and incomplete numerical reconciliation: Table 9 retains ±17, and Figure 6 does not explain differing accuracies at a nominally shared coefficient setting. The improvement is primarily in documentation and assessability.
